title: Current-mirror OTA
description: A current-mirror OTA, also called a symmetrical OTA or a current-amplifier OTA: the input pair drives diode-connected PMOS mirror loads, and each mirror is copied with ratio $K_m$ to an output branch — one side straight to the output, the other down through a bottom NMOS mirror — so the effective output transconductance is $K_m*g_{m,in}$ to first order. This buys bandwidth and slew almost for free — GBW = $K_m*g_{m,in}/(2*\pi*C_L)$ and SR = $K_m*I_{tail}/C_L$, to the same order — but not DC gain: raising $K_m$ scales both the output transconductance and the output conductance together, so the low-frequency gain is nearly independent of $K_m$. The amplifier is drawn at rest: the feedback the application closes around it holds the output at $V_{out,dc}$, and the two inputs sit apart by whatever offset that takes. The mirrors are stated the way the circuit has them: each output device sits on its diode device's gate at a multiple of that device's width, and its current is read from the table at its own drain voltage. Nothing is trimmed to make a copy exact, so the ratios the rows report are $K_m$ moved by each mirror's drain-voltage error, and the two output devices would not carry the same current if the two sides of the pair did. One current is typed — the tail current, into a diode-connected bias reference — and every other device reads another device's current or takes it through a shared gate: the tail device sits on that reference's gate at that reference's width with the tail node as its drain; the pair's two transistors are one width, and so are the two PMOS diode devices, each side carrying its own share of what the tail delivers. The share is solved so that the currents at the output node balance — the PMOS output device sources exactly what the NMOS one sinks — and the difference between the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages is reported as the systematic offset. One node is solved besides the tail node and the share: the NMOS diode's, which sits at that diode's own gate-source voltage at the current the PMOS output device above it delivers there. The catch of the topology shows up in noise: to hit a fixed GBW at larger $K_m$ the input pair shrinks ($g_{m,in}$ falls as $1/K_m$), so its input-referred thermal density grows as $\sqrt{K_m}$. Two mirror nodes carry poles: the PMOS node every branch passes (a full pole), and the bottom NMOS node only the folded branch passes (a pole-zero doublet). Both estimates are shown; settling is sim-owned.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. With every mirror device counted and each device's noise read from the tables, the row lands near 35 nV/rtHz on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table — over this budget. No simulated floor exists for this topology. Meeting this budget on silicon takes a lower K_m, lower gm/ID on the mirrors, or more current in the pair

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the vds of the two mirror output devices that meet at the output. They push and pull against each other at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here, and the share of the tail current each side of the pair carries is what balances them at this level

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low end — checked exactly by the cm-lo range end at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.96-1.41 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices, the low end set by the tail device leaving saturation). The range end checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source and the tail device's drain. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage, and the tail device's drain-source voltage, in one stroke. Above the diode-loaded drain (VDD minus the mirror's |vgs|) the pair has no drain-source voltage. An end of the range where the relation does not evaluate is stepped inward silently, and the searched range is reported only if the search then fails

params.name: V_nmir
params.note: the NMOS diode's node — the gate and drain of the bottom mirror's diode device, and the drain of the PMOS output device that feeds it. Solved, not set: that PMOS device's drain-source voltage is what is left between the supply and this node, the current it delivers there is the current the diode carries, and the diode's own gate-source voltage at that current is this node. The engine searches for the node at which the two agree; the stored value is never read. It is searched between its two neighbours, ground and the 1.8 V supply

params.name: out_share
params.note: the share of the tail current the pair transistor on the output-driving side carries at rest — solved, not set. The output is a high-impedance node that the feedback around the amplifier holds at V_out_dc, so in the resting circuit what the PMOS output device sources is exactly what the NMOS output device sinks: the engine searches for the share at which the two are equal, the current law at the output node. The other side carries the rest, so the two add up to what the tail delivers by construction. It is searched between 0.01 and 0.99; the stored value is never read

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. Only the two PMOS output devices read it — a diode device's drain follows its own gate in whichever convention its table uses. Read all four PMOS devices from the same table: the gate voltage they share is passed in that table's convention

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node normally sits below the reference's diode drop). Each side of the pair carries half of what the tail delivers and every mirror output device takes its current through the gate it shares, so transconductance, slew rate and supply current are computed from what the devices deliver, not from this number

params.name: K_m
params.note: mirror ratio, as a width ratio: each PMOS output device is K_m times its diode device's width on the same gate. Multiplies GBW and SR, but raises input noise as sqrt(K_m) at fixed GBW. The current ratio a mirror delivers differs from K_m by that mirror's drain-voltage error

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion, set on the transistor on the output-driving side; its partner copies its width and carries the rest of the tail current. Sets gm per current and the input-referred noise floor

params.name: gm_id_ml
params.note: mirror inversion, set on the PMOS diode device on the output-driving side and on the bottom NMOS diode, and inherited by each output device through the gate it shares (the other PMOS diode device copies the first one's width): sets the mirror-node poles, and lower gm/ID gives the output devices a higher output resistance

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: higher V* costs CM-low headroom

params.name: L_mir
params.note: length of every mirror device — a diode device and the output devices on its gate mirror at one length: longer shrinks each mirror's drain-voltage error and raises the output resistance

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input mirror device (diode), output-driving side
doc.description: Diode-connected mirror load on the side whose mirror drives the output directly, carrying that side's share of what the tail delivers, read from the tail device rather than typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated; its gate node carries the mirror pole. It publishes its width, which the other side's diode device copies, and its gate voltage, which the PMOS output device at the output copies.

doc.title: Input-pair device, output-driving side
doc.description: The pair transistor under the output-driving side's diode device, sized at that side's share of what the tail delivers; the diode device above it is in the same branch and carries the same current. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain one diode drop below the supply, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the two. It publishes its width, which its partner copies, and its gate-source voltage, which differs from its partner's by the input offset that holds the output where it is.

doc.title: Input mirror device (diode), folded side
doc.description: Diode-connected mirror load on the side whose mirror feeds the bottom mirror: the other diode device's width, carrying the rest of what the tail delivers. Its drain is its gate, so the table is read along that diagonal at that current for the gate-source voltage it takes. It publishes its gate voltage, which the PMOS output device feeding the bottom mirror copies.

params.name: W_m
params.note: the other diode device's width — a matched pair

doc.title: Input-pair device, folded side
doc.description: The pair transistor under the folded side's diode device: the other transistor's width, carrying the rest of what the tail delivers. A matched pair is one width, so its width is copied, and its current is given, which makes this a width-and-current sizing: the table is inverted at that current density for the gate-source voltage it takes. Its body bias is the tail node and its drain one diode drop below the supply. Wherever its current differs from its partner's, so does its gate-source voltage, and that difference is the input offset the sheet reports.

params.name: W_i
params.note: the other transistor's width — a matched pair

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side)
doc.description: The PMOS mirror's output device at the output node: $K_m$ times the diode device's width on the diode device's gate. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the diode device sits at its own gate-source voltage and this device at $V_{DD} - V_{out,dc}$, so it delivers $K_m$ times the diode's current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. Its gds is one half of the output conductance and its gate cap loads the mirror node.

params.name: W_o
params.note: K_m times the diode device's width

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share, in the sign convention of the diode device's table

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the supply down to the output, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side, feeding the bottom mirror)
doc.description: The other PMOS mirror's output device: $K_m$ times the folded side's diode device's width on that device's gate, with its drain on the NMOS diode's node instead of at the output. It sits at $V_{DD} - V_{nmir}$, not at the output's drain voltage, so it delivers a different current from the device at the output, and that current is what the bottom mirror is handed. Its drain voltage and the current it delivers there set each other through the NMOS diode below it, which is the one loop this sheet closes.

params.name: W_o
params.note: K_m times the diode device's width

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share, in the sign convention of the diode device's table

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the supply down to the NMOS diode's node, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Bottom mirror device (NMOS diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected NMOS that folds the second branch down to the bottom output device: one input branch reaches the output through its PMOS mirror alone, the other continues through this device to moutn. It carries the current the PMOS output device above it delivers, read from that device rather than typed; its gate node is the second mirror pole. Diode-connected, so its drop is read off the vds = vgs diagonal — and that drop is the node the PMOS device above it has its drain on. It publishes its width and its gate voltage for the bottom output device to copy.

doc.title: Output mirror device (NMOS side)
doc.description: The bottom mirror's output device: the NMOS diode device's width on the NMOS diode device's gate, a 1:1 copy with its drain at the output. Its current is read off the table at $V_{out,dc}$ rather than typed. It is a copy of a copy, so it carries the drain-voltage error of both mirrors in its path, and what it sinks differs from what the PMOS device at the output sources. Its gds is the other half of the output conductance.

params.name: W_o
params.note: the NMOS diode device's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the NMOS diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the output level

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting: the tail node plus the mean of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages, the level the two inputs sit about. It rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: Ai_p
equations.note: small-signal current gain of the PMOS mirror that drives the output directly: the output device's gm over its diode device's. It is the width ratio K_m moved by the difference between the two drain voltages

equations.name: Ai_n
equations.note: small-signal current gain of the path through the bottom mirror: the other PMOS mirror's gain times the NMOS mirror's. Two copies in series, so it carries two drain-voltage errors

equations.name: Gm_out
equations.note: output transconductance. Each pair transistor turns half the differential input into current at its own $g_m$, and each half reaches the output through its own mirror path: the output-driving side's through its PMOS mirror, gain Ai_p, the folded side's through both mirrors, gain Ai_n. It is K_m times the input $g_m$ where the two sides sit at the same levels and both paths copy exactly

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output node loaded by the conductance of both output devices, each read where its mirror puts it: on its diode device's gate, at the output's drain voltage. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: DC gain; K_m scales Gm_out and (via the K_m-wider output devices) Rout inversely, so gain is nearly K_m-independent

equations.name: GBW
equations.note: dominant-pole gain-bandwidth into the load, from the transconductance the two mirror paths deliver

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered to one side of the pair is twice what that side carries at rest, so the output device at the end of that side's mirror path delivers twice its quiescent current to first order. Rising, that is the PMOS output device; falling, the NMOS one. The two differ by the mirrors' drain-voltage errors, and this is the slower direction

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: every device that puts noise current into the output, each at its own density, referred to the input through the path it takes. A device's density times its gm is its drain noise current, and a noise current at the output divided by Gm_out is an input voltage. The two input devices: a pair device's noise current splits evenly between the two sides at the tail node and reaches the output through both mirror paths, exactly as the signal does, so each counts once at its own density. The two PMOS diode devices, each at its own current: one is copied to the output by its mirror, gain Ai_p, the other through both mirrors, gain Ai_n. The PMOS output device at the output and the NMOS output device put their noise current straight into the output. The PMOS output device that feeds the bottom mirror and the NMOS diode device under it put theirs into the NMOS diode's node, and the bottom mirror copies it to the output with its own gain, gm_moutn/gm_nmir. The tail device and its bias reference are left out: their noise reaches both sides equally and cancels at the output to first order

equations.name: vn_gbw
equations.note: estimate: the input pair's own share of the input density if the pair were sized to just meet GBW_target at this K_m — grows as sqrt(K_m), the current-mirror OTA's noise-for-bandwidth trade. Each pair device's channel noise against its gm, 4kT*gamma*(gm + gmb)/gm, is read off the input device at its own bias as in__svth_m*in__gm, so the table's own noise and the body effect follow. The mirror devices add to it, as the vn_in row counts

equations.name: f_pole
equations.note: estimate: the PMOS mirror-node pole, set by the diode device's gm over its own gate cap plus that of the K_m-times-wider output device on the same node. Read on the side that drives the output; the other side's node carries a device of the same width at a different drain voltage

equations.name: f_pole_n
equations.note: estimate: the bottom NMOS mirror-node pole, same accounting as f_pole on the folded branch: the diode device's gm, at the current it is handed, over its own gate cap plus that of the equal-width output device

equations.name: PM
equations.note: estimate: the two mirror nodes cost phase differently, because the signal reaches them differently. BOTH input branches pass a PMOS mirror node, so $f_{pole}$ is a full pole in the whole path — unlike the 5T's mirror. Only the folded branch passes the bottom NMOS mirror, so half the signal is delayed there and $f_{pole,n}$ is a pole-ZERO DOUBLET (zero at twice the pole), costing far less phase. Measured against the ACHIEVED GBW, so overshooting the bandwidth target spends margin honestly

equations.name: vos_sys
equations.note: input-referred systematic offset — the difference of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages at rest, read directly: the input offset the feedback holding the output at $V_{out,dc}$ has to apply. The output node takes the PMOS output device's current in and the NMOS output device's current out; each is a copy made at a drain voltage that is not its diode device's, and the NMOS one is a copy of a copy, so at an even split the two would not carry the same current. The share is solved so that they do, and the two pair transistors then carry different currents and need different gate-source voltages. Reported only; no check reads it

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact here, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single pair transistor, as the mean of the two, which differ a little because their currents do. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the current the tail device delivers, which the two input branches carry down from the supply through their PMOS diode devices, plus the branches of the two PMOS output devices, each at the current that device delivers at its own drain voltage. The bottom mirror adds nothing: it carries to ground current already counted on the PMOS side. The reference branch that programs the tail is shared bias infrastructure, typically one reference feeding several stages, and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
estimate: margin left at crossover once the mirror node is paid for; advisory, since an open-loop OTA needs none of it and sim owns the real stability

checks.lhs: min(VDD - abs(mload__vgs) - V_tail - in__vdsat, VDD - abs(mload_f__vgs) - V_tail - in_f__vdsat)
checks.note: trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the diode load — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less diode drop
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges check that the design covers the range ENDS, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve over its full range, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
